text:
support_anna: Hey team, AcmeCorp in private VPC reporting NLB target showing Unhealthy after a config push. App logs show TLS handshake errors and AWS console shows NLB health check failing with connection resets. Customer says this started after enabling client IP forwarding on the LB.

infra_mike: Can you paste the NLB listener / target group settings? health check protocol/port, and whether Proxy Protocol is enabled on the listener?

support_anna: Sure, from the console: 
- Listener: TCP 8443 -> target group (instances)
- Health check: TCP 8443, interval 10s, healthy 3 / unhealthy 2
- Listener attribute: Proxy Protocol V2 = Enabled (we enabled to preserve client IPs)

customer_ops: Attaching a trimmed tcpdump from the app node. You can see the NLB injecting a PROXY v2 header before the TLS ClientHello, app expects TLS immediately and logs look like TLS record parsing errors.

```
17:23:45.123456 IP 100.64.1.35.52344 > 10.0.5.12.8443: Flags [P.], seq 1:123, ack 1, win 65535
Payload: PROXY TCP4 10.0.2.11 192.0.2.50 52344 8443\r\n\x16\x03\x01\x02\x00... (TLS ClientHello bytes follow)
```

eng_jia: This is a classic proxy-protocol mismatch. If NLB sends PROXY headers but the app/Envoy/ingress controller isn't configured to parse PROXY v2, the extra bytes will break the TLS handshake. The server reads the PROXY header bytes as if they were TLS and errors with something like `ssl3_get_record:wrong version number`.

infra_mike: Quick repro steps I ran locally:
1) `printf 'PROXY TCP4 10.0.2.11 192.0.2.50 52344 8443\r\n' | nc -q 1 <target_ip> 8443` -> server resets / TLS handshake fails.
2) Disable Proxy Protocol on the NLB listener -> healthcheck succeeds and target goes Healthy within ~20s.

eng_jia: Two remediation paths:
- Enable PROXY v2 parsing in the ingress/Envoy (recommended if you need client IPs) — e.g., in Envoy config set `use_proxy_proto: true` on the listener or enable `proxy_protocol` in the ingress annotations so Envoy accepts v2.
- Or disable Proxy Protocol on the NLB listener so the app sees raw TLS client hello directly.

support_anna: We tested both. Customer chose to enable proxy parsing in their custom ingress config (they had a managed Envoy but parsing was off). After enabling PROXY v2 on the ingress and restarting pods the TLS errors stopped and AWS shows Healthy.

customer_ops: Logs after the fix show parsed proxy metadata and successful TLS handshake: `PROXY src=10.0.2.11 dst=192.0.2.50 sport=52344 dport=8443` then `TLS handshake complete`.

infra_mike: Root cause summary for runbook: NLB was configured to emit PROXY protocol v2 for client IP preservation, but target (Envoy/ingress or app) wasn't configured to parse PROXY headers -> proxied bytes broke TLS handshake -> health checks failed.

eng_jia: Notes and followups:
- Add a check in our private deploy playbook to verify `proxy_protocol` parity between LB and target.
- Consider adding a diagnostic script (curl/openssl/nc combo) we can run during oncall to quickly detect PROXY mismatch.
- We should also document the specific Envoy annotation and a minimal config snippet for customers.

deploy-bot: Change applied: disabled NLB proxy_protocol on listener tcp/8443 for tg-0a1b2c. (timing: 2026-08-21T17:28:45Z) :white_check_mark:

support_anna: Thanks all — customer confirmed full recovery and we're closing the escalation. I'll add the runbook note and example `openssl`/`printf | nc` probes to the support diagnostics doc. :thumbsup:
